title: Gentiopicroside Ameliorates Psoriasis-Like Dermatitis by Modulating Immune Homeostasis and Suppressing NF-kappaB Activation.
authors: Du, Lingyun; Zhao, Xiaoke; Wei, Jingjing; Lv, Shanrong; Li, Mingming; Leng, Yi; Yu, Kemei; Xu, Qingqing; Zhang, Chunhong
one_liner_zh: 该文研究龙胆苦苷通过免疫调节和抑制NF-kappaB信号改善银屑病，仅用分子对接预测小分子与NF-kappaB p65结合，非蛋白质-DNA互作体系，且无AI/物理模拟方法，与本课题关系微弱。
abstract: Psoriasis is a common chronic immune-mediated inflammatory skin disease that presents significant challenges in clinical management. Gentiopicroside (GPS), a bioactive compound derived from Gentiana scabra, has been reported to possess anti-inflammatory and immunomodulatory properties. However, its potential role in the treatment of psoriasis remains unclear. This study aimed to investigate the therapeutic effects of GPS on psoriasis-like dermatitis and elucidate its underlying mechanisms. A psoriasis-like dermatitis model was established in BALB/c mice using imiquimod (IMQ). The therapeutic efficacy of GPS was evaluated based on clinical and histopathological improvements. Flow cytometry was used to analyze immune cell populations in the spleen and peripheral blood. In vitro, the effects of GPS on bone marrow-derived dendritic cells (BMDCs) were assessed in an inflammatory model. RNA sequencing was performed to identify differentially expressed genes and key signaling pathways in BMDCs after GPS treatment. Molecular docking was employed to predict the binding affinity between GPS and potential targets, which were further validated using Western blotting and immunofluorescence. GPS treatment significantly alleviated psoriasis-like skin lesions in IMQ-induced mice, improving both clinical manifestations and histopathological alterations. GPS reduced the proportions of lymphocytes and dendritic cells and attenuated Th17-driven inflammation, thereby contributing to a more balanced immune milieu. In vitro, GPS inhibited the maturation and activation of BMDCs. Transcriptomic profiling demonstrated that GPS modulated multiple immune- and cytokine-associated pathways, particularly the NF-kappaB signaling pathway. Molecular docking suggested a strong binding affinity between GPS and NF-kappaB p65, while Western blotting and immunofluorescence confirmed that GPS suppressed phosphorylated NF-kappaB p65 nuclear translocation. GPS exerts anti-psoriatic effects through multimodal mechanisms, including immunomodulation and suppression of NF-kappaB activation. These findings provide experimental evidence and a theoretical basis for the development of GPS as a potential therapeutic agent for psoriasis.
abstract_zh: 银屑病是一种常见的慢性免疫介导的炎症性皮肤病，在临床管理中面临重大挑战。龙胆苦苷（GPS），一种源自龙胆（Gentiana scabra）的生物活性化合物，已被报道具有抗炎和免疫调节特性。然而，其在银屑病治疗中的潜在作用仍不明确。本研究旨在探讨GPS对银屑病样皮炎的治疗效果，并阐明其潜在机制。使用咪喹莫特（IMQ）在BALB/c小鼠中建立银屑病样皮炎模型。基于临床和组织病理学改善评估GPS的治疗效果。采用流式细胞术分析脾脏和外周血中的免疫细胞群体。在体外，评估GPS对骨髓来源树突状细胞（BMDCs）在炎症模型中的影响。进行RNA测序以鉴定GPS处理后BMDCs中的差异表达基因和关键信号通路。采用分子对接预测GPS与潜在靶点之间的结合亲和力，并通过Western blotting和免疫荧光进一步验证。GPS治疗显著缓解了IMQ诱导小鼠的银屑病样皮肤病变，改善了临床表现和组织病理学改变。GPS降低了淋巴细胞和树突状细胞的比例，并减弱了Th17驱动的炎症，从而有助于形成更平衡的免疫环境。在体外，GPS抑制了BMDCs的成熟和活化。转录组分析表明，GPS调节了多种免疫和细胞因子相关通路，特别是NF-kappaB信号通路。分子对接提示GPS与NF-kappaB p65之间具有强结合亲和力，而Western blotting和免疫荧光证实GPS抑制了磷酸化NF-kappaB p65的核转位。GPS通过多模式机制发挥抗银屑病作用，包括免疫调节和抑制NF-kappaB激活。这些发现为GPS作为银屑病潜在治疗药物的开发提供了实验证据和理论基础。
